proof_summary: Fixed bounded digit-sum sets have density zero, via an \(O((\log N)^B)\) counting bound; splitting by the last two digits then shows every competing value has limsup frequency at most \(1/100\), since only numbers ending in \(99\) remain non-negligible. Conversely, numbers \(10t+9\) with \(t\) not ending in \(9\) and with digit sum at least \(8\) yield the distinguished value, giving limsup frequency at least \(1/100\) along cutoffs \(100K\).
